chunks: From him, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from Abu Talib, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), the first [Imam], 'I have farms and dwellings between one village and two or three [villages].' He said, 'For every dwelling among your dwellings that you do not make your permanent residence, you must offer the shortening of prayer (qasr) in it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prayer for someone who owns multiple homes within a short distance?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the criterion for 'traveler status' (musafir) regarding prayer shortening, establishing that ownership of multiple residences within the distance of qasr does not negate travel if one does not permanently inhabit any single one. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that the intent and actual pattern of residence, rather than mere property ownership, determine the applicability of the concession. This ruling is foundational in the chapters of Salah al-Safar within the Tahdhib al-Ahkam, reflecting the practical legal reasoning of the Imams.
